answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a beacon-tended orchard of standing. Each identity grows a vine of reputation only by answering unpredictable beacon challenges in narrow windows across consecutive epochs, each answer chained to the last, so progress cannot be bought in bulk or run in parallel. A vine that misses its window is pruned back to a seedling, and only vines surviving a full season earn attestation weight. Tending ten fake identities then means tending ten separate vines through ten separate seasons, which costs ten times the calendar time, not ten times a fee.
